pages.title: Week 1: Intro to P.E.
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.1 · Intro to P.E.
Week 1

You Are a Movement Superstar! 🌟

Welcome to PE, friend! Get ready to run, jump, dance, stretch, and discover what your amazing body can do. This week, we're talking about why moving is awesome — for your body, your brain, and your friendships.

1
Lesson 1
Why Move Your Body?

Quick quiz: Have you ever played tag? Danced to your favorite song? Ridden a bike, or chased a friend across the playground?

BOOM 💥 — that was physical activity! Physical activity is any time you move your body in a way that gets your heart pumping and your muscles working. And here's the cool part: you don't have to be an athlete to do it. Every single human on Earth needs to move every day. That includes YOU. 🎉

2
Lesson 2
What Happens Inside Your Body When You Move?

When you run, jump, stretch, or climb — something magical happens inside you. Let's peek under the hood! 🚗

❤️
Your Heart
Becomes a super-strong pump that sends blood (and oxygen!) zooming around your body.
🫁
Your Lungs
Pull in WAY more oxygen so your body has the fuel it needs to keep playing.
💪
Your Muscles
Grow stronger so you can carry, climb, and play harder without getting tired.
🦴
Your Bones
Get TOUGHER, like superhero armor for your insides.
💡Did You Know?

Your heart beats about 100,000 times every single day — even when you're sleeping! When you exercise, it beats even faster to get extra oxygen to your muscles. Try this: put your hand on your chest right now. Feel that bump-bump? That's your heart saying hi! 💓

3
Lesson 3
Moving = Happy Feelings

Here's a secret most kids don't know: moving your body changes how you FEEL on the inside too.

When you're active, your brain makes special chemicals called endorphins (en-DOR-fins) — they're like tiny happiness sparkles for your mind. ✨ Moving can make you feel:

  • 😄 Happier — like everything is just a little brighter
  • 😌 Calmer — your worries shrink down small
  • 🎯 More focused — your brain is ready to learn at school
  • 😴 Sleepier at bedtime — in a good way!
🌎Real-World Connection

Real talk: Ever notice how recess makes you feel awesome? Or how a quick dance break wakes you up when you're tired? That's not magic — that's your body and brain working together because you MOVED. 🎮 You can use this power any time you feel grumpy or stuck. Just take 2 minutes to wiggle, hop, or stretch and watch what happens!

4
Lesson 4
Movement Builds Friendships

PE isn't just about getting strong — it's also about getting CLOSE with the people around you. When you play games, dance, or do activities with others, you practice:

  • 🤝 Teamwork — figuring out how to win together
  • 📜 Following rules so the game is fair for everyone
  • 😂 Laughing, sharing, and cheering each other on

Being a good teammate is a skill you can practice your whole life — and it starts right here in PE.

💭Think About It

Think about a time you played with a friend and it felt SUPER fun. What made it fun? Was it the game, the people, the silliness, or all three? 💭

5
Lesson 5
Movement Words to Know

🎯 Your Movement Vocabulary

  • Movement — When your body changes position (walking, jumping, dancing).
  • Balance — Staying steady so you don't tip over (like standing on one foot 🦩).
  • Coordination — When your brain and body team up to move smoothly.
  • Strength — When your muscles can push, pull, lift, or carry stuff.
  • Endurance — How long you can keep going without pooping out.
  • Teamwork — Working with others to reach the same goal.
📝Weekly Reflection

Quick Reflection Time! 📝

Tell me about the LAST time you moved your body and felt awesome. What were you doing? Who was there? How did you feel after? (Bonus points if you describe the silliest move you made this week. 😜)

→What's Next

Next up: Week 1 Discussion — share your favorite ways to move with your classmates. Then it's time to set up your first Movement Stations activity!

pages.title: Flight Club Guidelines 🦉
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.1 · Intro to P.E.
Flight Club

Welcome to Flight Club 🦉🚀

Buckle up, future flyer! Flight Club is where you earn points by completing weekly movement challenges. The more you challenge yourself, the higher you'll climb the ranks. Are you ready to take flight?

1
How It Works
The Basics

Each week brings new Flight Club challenges — stretching, strength, balance, and movement activities for you to complete. Every time you finish a challenge, you earn Flight Points.

Your goal? Rack up points over the year and rise to the highest rank!

  • 🎯 Maximum score: 100 points
  • 🏆 5 ranks to climb (lowest to highest)
  • 🌟 Bonus points for completing every challenge in a month
2
The Ranks
From Nestling to Soaring Owl 🦉
🌌
Soaring Owl
(85–100 pts)
The top tier! You've mastered movement and you fly above the rest. Legendary!
🦉
Wise Owl
(70–84 pts)
Strong, focused, and skilled. You're a top flyer.
🪽
Gliding Owl
(50–69 pts)
Smooth flying! Keep going — Soaring Owl is in sight.
🐤
Fluttering Owl
(30–49 pts)
You've taken off! Keep practicing to build your wings.
🥚
Nestling Learner
(0–29 pts)
Just starting — that's perfect! Every challenge helps you grow.
3
Earning Points
How to Rack Them Up

💪 Daily Stretch Challenge

5 points per stretch you complete.

🌟 Perfect Monthly Participation

10 bonus points if you finish ALL of the challenges in a month!

🎓 End-of-Year Bonus

At the end of the course, your rank earns extra credit toward your final grade!

💡Did You Know?

Owls have AMAZING flexibility — they can turn their heads almost all the way around! Their flight is silent because of special feathers. Every Flight Club rank is named after these awesome athletes of the sky. 🦉

🌎Real-World Connection

This isn't about being the strongest or fastest kid in class. It's about YOUR progress. Every challenge you complete is a victory — and every Owl rank is something to be proud of. 🌟

4
Get Started
Your Mission

Look for "Flight Club" challenges in your weekly modules. They'll always have the bright pink Flight Club Challenge badge so you can spot them easily!

Each challenge tells you exactly what to do. Just complete it, submit your proof (video or guardian note), and watch your points add up. 📈

📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: What rank would you be PROUD to reach this year? What's your first step? 📝

→What's Next

Time to fly! Look for your first Flight Club challenge in this week's module. Let's GO! 🚀

pages.title: Week 3: Warm-Ups & Cool-Downs
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.2 · Warm-Ups & Cool-Downs
Week 3

Warm-Ups & Cool-Downs: Power On, Power Off ⚡

Imagine starting a race car engine on a freezing morning and immediately flooring it. BAD IDEA. Your body is the same way! Before you go full speed, you need to warm up. And after you're done? Your body needs a cool-down to recharge.

1
Lesson 1
What's a Warm-Up?

A warm-up is when you do gentle movements BEFORE a workout, game, or PE activity to wake your body up. It's like saying, "Hey muscles! Hey heart! Hey lungs! We're about to have FUN — get ready!" 🔥

A good warm-up:

  • Wakes up your muscles so they're stretchy and ready
  • Tells your heart to start pumping a little faster
  • Helps you focus on the activity
  • Keeps you from getting hurt 🩹
2
Lesson 2
What's a Cool-Down?

A cool-down is the OPPOSITE — gentle movements AFTER activity that help your body slow down on purpose. Think of it like landing an airplane gently instead of crashing it. ✈️

When you cool down:

  • Your breathing returns to normal 🫁
  • Your heart rate slows back down ❤️‍🩹
  • Your muscles relax and get stretched
  • You feel less sore the next day!
💡Did You Know?

If you skip your cool-down and just plop down after running hard, the blood in your legs can pool there and make you feel dizzy! Cool-downs literally help your blood flow back to your heart the smart way. 🩸 Cool, right?

3
Try It
5 Warm-Up Moves to Try Today
💪
Arm Circles
10 seconds forward, 10 seconds backward.
🦘
High Knees
March in place, lifting knees high — 15 seconds.
🔄
Shoulder Rolls
5 forward, 5 backward. Loose like a noodle.
🦶
Toe Touches
Reach down toward your toes — 10 seconds.
🏃
Jog in Place
Easy bouncy jog — 30 seconds. You should feel a little out of breath!
🏃Activity Cue

Check yourself: "Do I feel ready to move?" If your answer is YES — go play! If your heart is still pretty chill, do one more move. 🏃

4
Try It
5 Cool-Down Stretches
🤗
Hug Yourself
Wrap arms around yourself — hold 10 seconds.
🦋
Butterfly Stretch
Sit, feet together, gently flap your knees like wings.
🌬️
Deep Breathing
In through the nose (4 counts), out through the mouth (4 counts).
🌟
Reach for the Sky
Arms way up high, then slowly lower.
🦵
Leg Stretch
Sit and reach toward your toes — gently!
✅Check for Understanding

Ask yourself: "Is my heart beating slower? Do I feel calm?" If yes, mission accomplished! 🎯 If you still feel hyped up, breathe deeply for 30 more seconds.

🌎Real-World Connection

Even pro athletes — basketball stars, gymnasts, soccer players — warm up AND cool down every single practice. If it's good enough for the pros, it's good enough for you. 🏆

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Warm-Up — Gentle movement that gets your body ready to play.
  • Cool-Down — Gentle movement after activity to help your body relax.
  • Stretch — Reaching your muscles so they stay long and loose.
  • Injury — When part of your body gets hurt.
  • Heart Rate — How fast your heart is beating.
  • Recovery — Letting your body relax and feel better after exercise.
📝Weekly Reflection

This Week's Reflection: Which warm-up move felt the silliest? Which cool-down made you feel the calmest? 📝

→What's Next

Up next: Week 3 Discussion with your classmates, then it's time to build your very own warm-up and cool-down routine in Week 4!

pages.title: Week 5: Muscular Strength
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.3 · Muscular Strength & Endurance
Week 5

Strength: Your Built-In Superpower 💪

You don't need to lift cars or bend metal to be strong. Strength means your muscles are powerful enough to help you do all the fun stuff you love — without getting wiped out. Let's unlock yours!

1
Lesson 1
What Even IS Strength?

Have you ever lifted your backpack and gone, "Whoa — this thing weighs a TON"? Or climbed up the jungle gym at recess? Or held a heavy door open for someone? That's strength in action!

Strength doesn't mean you have giant muscles like a cartoon superhero 🦸. It means your muscles can:

  • Push things 🔃
  • Pull things ⬅️➡️
  • Lift things ⬆️
  • Carry things 🎒
  • Hold a position (like a plank or a yoga pose)
2
Lesson 2
Why Do YOU Need Strength?

Spoiler: you already use strength every single day!

🎒
Carrying Stuff
Your school bag, lunch box, instruments.
🪜
Climbing Stairs
Your leg muscles power you up every step.
🪑
Sitting Up Straight
Your core (tummy & back muscles) hold you up.
🧹
Helping at Home
Sweeping, carrying laundry, lifting groceries.
💡Did You Know?

You have over 600 muscles in your body! Every time you smile, you're using about 17 of them. Every time you laugh REALLY hard, you're working out your tummy muscles. 😂 So technically, laughing IS exercise!

3
Lesson 3
How Do You Build Strength?

Here's the best news ever: you don't need a gym or fancy weights. The best strength tool in the world is your own body!

👐
Push-Ups
Strengthen arms, shoulders, and chest.
🦵
Squats
Power up your legs for running and jumping.
🪵
Planks
Build a strong core for balance and posture.
🐒
Monkey Bars
Climbing builds your grip and shoulder strength.
🏃Activity Cue

Try this right now: Stand up, then sit back down. Stand up, sit back down. Do this 10 times in a row. THAT'S a strength workout! Your legs just did a mini squat session. 🦵

🌎Real-World Connection

Think about your favorite athletes — basketball players, dancers, soccer stars, even YouTubers doing parkour. Every single one of them does strength training. Strong muscles = more energy, fewer injuries, and longer playtime. 🏆

4
Lesson 4
Strong Body = Happy You

When your muscles are strong, you feel different — in a good way. You have more energy. You bounce back faster. You're more confident when you try new stuff. And — bonus — your body protects itself better when you fall or trip. 🩹

Remember: you don't have to be the strongest kid in class. You just have to keep moving and trying. Little by little, strength shows up. ✨

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Muscular Strength — How much power your muscles can produce.
  • Push — Using muscles to move something AWAY from you.
  • Pull — Using muscles to move something TOWARD you.
  • Core — The muscles in your tummy and back that keep you steady.
  • Posture — How you hold your body when you stand or sit.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflection time! 📝 What's the heaviest thing YOU have lifted this week? Was it easier or harder than you thought? What part of your body did most of the work?

→What's Next

Up next: Week 5 Discussion, then in Week 6 you'll choose your favorite ways to show off your strength!

pages.title: Week 7: Cardiovascular Fitness
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.4 · Cardiovascular Fitness
Week 7

Cardio: The Engine That Powers YOU 🏃💨

Your heart and lungs are basically a team — and when they work together to move oxygen around your body, that's called cardiovascular fitness. The more you use them, the stronger they get. Let's fire up the engine!

1
Lesson 1
What IS Cardiovascular Fitness?

Have you ever played tag, jumped rope, or sprinted across the playground and felt your heart go BOOM-BOOM-BOOM? 💓 That's your cardiovascular system doing its job!

"Cardio" comes from the word heart. "Vascular" is about your blood vessels (the tubes that carry blood around your body). So cardiovascular fitness = how well your heart and lungs work TOGETHER to keep you moving.

Any activity that gets your heart pumping faster counts as cardio: running, dancing, biking, swimming, skipping — even chasing your dog around the yard. 🐕

2
Lesson 2
What Happens to Your Body During Cardio?
❤️
Heart Gets Stronger
It's a muscle — and like every muscle, it grows tougher when you use it.
🫁
Lungs Pull In More Oxygen
So you can play longer without getting tired.
🩸
Blood Flows Better
Delivering fuel to your brain and muscles.
🔋
Endurance Goes UP
You can keep going and going — like a power bar that never drains.
💡Did You Know?

Your blood travels about 12,000 MILES every single day through your body. That's like going from coast to coast across America FOUR TIMES! When you do cardio, your blood moves even faster. 🚀

3
Lesson 3
How Does Cardio Make You FEEL?

Cardio doesn't just make your body strong — it gives your brain a glow-up too. 🌟

  • 😄 You feel happier and more confident
  • 🎯 You focus better at school
  • 😴 You sleep WAY better at night
  • 😌 Stress melts away
  • ⚡ You have more energy for everything else you love
🌎Real-World Connection

Ever feel like you've got the wiggles and can't sit still? That's a sign your body is asking for cardio! Try 30 seconds of jumping jacks or running in place — and watch your wiggles turn into focus. 🎯

4
Lesson 4
Cardio Can Be SO Fun

Cardio doesn't have to mean running laps until you drop. Try these:

💃
Dance Party
Crank your favorite song and GO.
🚴
Bike Ride
Around the block, in the park, anywhere.
🏀
Sports With Friends
Basketball, soccer, four-square.
🪜
Obstacle Courses
Make one in your living room or backyard.
🏃Activity Cue

Try this: Right now, do 20 jumping jacks. Then put your hand on your chest. Feel that BOOM-BOOM-BOOM? That's cardio! Your heart just got a tiny workout. 🎉

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Cardiovascular — Anything about your heart and blood vessels.
  • Heart Rate — How fast your heart is beating (counted in beats per minute).
  • Endurance — How long your body can keep moving without getting tired.
  • Oxygen — The part of the air your body needs to make energy.
  • Energy — What your body uses to move, play, and think.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflection: What's YOUR favorite way to do cardio? When was the last time you felt your heart pound? Describe how your body felt during AND after. 📝

→What's Next

Coming next: Week 7 Discussion, then in Week 8 you'll create your very own 10-minute cardio routine!

pages.title: Week 9: Flexibility & Stretching
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.5 · Flexibility & Stretching
Week 9

Flexibility: Bend, Twist, Stretch — Like a Superhero 🤸

Ever try to tie your shoes and... ouch? Or reach for something on a high shelf and your back goes "no thanks"? You might need more flexibility! Stretching keeps your body smooth, comfy, and ready for anything.

1
Lesson 1
What IS Flexibility?

Flexibility means your body can bend, twist, and stretch easily. It's about how far your joints (the places where your bones meet, like your knees and elbows) can move without pain.

When your muscles are flexible, you move like a graceful cat 🐈 instead of a creaky robot 🤖.

Flexible bodies can:

  • Run and jump without getting hurt
  • Sit comfortably without getting stiff
  • Balance better during sports and games
  • Move in all directions safely
2
Lesson 2
What Happens When You Stretch?

When you stretch, your muscles get a little longer and more relaxed — like rubber bands waking up. 🪢

🔥
Warms You Up
Gets blood flowing to your muscles.
🛡️
Prevents Injuries
Loose muscles don't pull as easily.
😌
Feels Amazing
Especially after a long day of sitting!
🦴
Helps Joints Move
Knees, hips, shoulders — all happier.
💡Did You Know?

Your body is most flexible right after you wake up... and least flexible when you're cold. That's why dancers, athletes, and gymnasts warm up BEFORE stretching. Always stretch a warm muscle, not a cold one! ☕

3
Lesson 3
How Flexibility Makes You Feel
  • 😌 Relaxed — like your body just took a deep breath
  • 🪶 Less tight — especially after sitting still for a long time
  • 💪 Proud — because you're taking care of your amazing body!
4
Try It
Make Stretching Fun

Stretching doesn't have to be boring. Try these:

⭐
Reach for the Stars
Stretch your arms WAY up like you're grabbing planets.
🐈
Cat Stretch
On hands and knees, arch and round your back.
🦩
Flamingo Stand
Lift one knee up, hold for 10 seconds. Switch!
🦋
Butterfly
Sit, feet together, gently bounce knees.
🏃Activity Cue

Try this: Stand up and slowly reach for the ceiling. Hold for 10 seconds. Now bend forward and try to touch your toes. Hold for 10 seconds. That's a stretch sandwich! 🥪

🌎Real-World Connection

Gymnasts, dancers, skateboarders, and martial artists ALL spend tons of time stretching. Why? Because flexibility helps them try cool tricks without getting hurt. The bendier you are, the more your body can do. 🤸

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Flexibility — How easily your body can bend, twist, and stretch.
  • Stretch — Gently pulling your muscles longer.
  • Muscles — The body parts that help you move.
  • Joint — Where two bones meet (knees, elbows, hips, shoulders).
  • Balance — Staying steady while standing or moving.
  • Warm-Up — Gentle movement to wake up your body.
📝Weekly Reflection

This week: Which stretch made you feel the BEST? Did anything feel surprisingly hard? Was there a body part you didn't know was so tight? 📝

→What's Next

Up next: Week 9 Discussion, then in Week 10 you'll design your own stretching guide!

pages.title: Week 11: Nutrition
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.6 · Nutrition
Week 11

Nutrition: You Are What You EAT 🍎

Your body is basically a super-cool machine — and food is its fuel! Just like a race car needs the right gas, your body needs the right food to run, learn, and play your best. Let's talk about what to put in your tank!

1
Lesson 1
What's Nutrition?

Nutrition is just a fancy word for the food and drinks your body needs to grow strong, stay healthy, and have ENERGY. ⚡

Think about it: how would your favorite video game character do if you forgot to give them power-ups? Probably not great. Your body works the same way — and the power-ups are real food. 🥦🍓🍞🥚🥛

2
Lesson 2
The 5 Food Groups

Healthy eating means getting a little something from each food group. Picture your plate like a team:

🥬
Vegetables
Power-ups full of vitamins. Broccoli, carrots, spinach!
🍎
Fruits
Sweet, natural energy. Apples, bananas, berries!
🍞
Grains
Long-lasting fuel. Bread, rice, pasta, oats.
🍗
Proteins
Muscle builders. Chicken, beans, eggs, nuts, fish.
🥛
Dairy
Strong bones! Milk, yogurt, cheese.
💡Did You Know?

Your body needs about 8 cups of water a day — that's why drinking water is just as important as eating! Your brain is about 75% water. Without enough, you can feel tired, grumpy, and have trouble focusing. So sip, sip, sip! 💧

3
Lesson 3
How Healthy Food Makes You Feel

When you eat a balanced meal (a little of each food group), here's what happens:

  • 🧠 Your brain stays sharp and ready to learn
  • 💪 Your muscles get stronger for moving and playing
  • ❤️ Your heart stays healthy
  • ⚡ Your energy lasts way longer
  • 😴 You sleep better at night
  • 🦠 You get sick less often
🌎Real-World Connection

Ever feel SUPER tired after eating a ton of candy? That's a "sugar crash" — your body got a quick burst of energy, then dropped fast. But fruits, veggies, and proteins give you energy that LASTS for hours. Way better for playing tag! 🏃

4
Lesson 4
You Don't Have to Be Perfect

Here's the truth: nobody eats perfectly every day. Pizza? Awesome. Cookies? Delicious. Birthday cake? YES PLEASE. 🎂

The goal isn't to NEVER eat treats. The goal is to make small healthy choices MOST of the time. Try things like:

  • Adding a fruit to breakfast 🍓
  • Choosing water with dinner 💧
  • Trying ONE new veggie this week 🥕
  • Helping make a meal at home 👨‍🍳
🏃Activity Cue

Challenge: Right now, name one food from EACH of the 5 groups that you actually like to eat. That's a healthy plate brain dump! 📝

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Nutrition — The food and drinks that help your body grow.
  • Energy — What your body uses to move, play, and think.
  • Balanced Meal — A meal with foods from different groups.
  • Protein — Builds and repairs muscles (meat, beans, eggs).
  • Vitamins — Tiny helpers in food that keep your body working.
  • Hydration — Drinking enough water.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflection time! 📝 What's the WEIRDEST food you've ever tried? Did you like it? What's one new healthy food you'd be brave enough to try this week?

→What's Next

Up next: Week 11 Discussion, then in Week 12 you'll design your own Healthy Plate masterpiece!

pages.title: Week 13: Locomotor Skills
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.7 · Locomotor Skills
Week 13

Locomotor Skills: How You GO 🚀

Walking, running, hopping, skipping — those are all "locomotor skills." It's just a fancy way of saying "the different ways your body moves from one place to another." And the more ways you can move, the more fun you can have!

1
Lesson 1
What's a Locomotor Skill?

The word locomotor comes from locomotive — which means a train engine. 🚂 Just like a train engine pulls a train down the track, your locomotor skills move YOU through the world.

Anytime you change spots — from the couch to the kitchen, or one end of the playground to the other — you're using a locomotor skill!

2
Lesson 2
The 8 Basic Locomotor Skills
🚶
Walking
The first one you ever learned. Smooth and steady.
🏃
Running
Faster, with a moment where BOTH feet are off the ground!
🦘
Jumping
Both feet leave the ground and land together.
🦩
Hopping
On ONE foot. Builds balance!
🎶
Skipping
Step-hop, step-hop. So fun!
🦒
Leaping
One BIG step off one foot, landing on the other.
🐴
Galloping
Like riding a pretend horse. One foot leads, the other follows.
⬅️➡️
Sliding
Sideways movement. Great for basketball defense!
💡Did You Know?

By the time you're 8 years old, your brain has practiced walking SO many times that it does it automatically — without you even thinking. But when you were a baby, you had to learn it from scratch. Your brain is incredible! 🧠

3
Lesson 3
Why Locomotor Skills Matter

The better you are at locomotor skills, the better you'll be at almost EVERY game and sport. Soccer? Running and sliding. Basketball? Running, jumping, sliding. Tag? ALL of them! 🎯

Plus, practicing different ways to move helps your brain too. It builds:

  • Balance (especially hopping and skipping)
  • Coordination (skipping and galloping are tricky!)
  • Spatial awareness — knowing where your body is in space so you don't bump into people 💥
🌎Real-World Connection

Dancers, athletes, and even astronauts practice locomotor skills. When astronauts come back from space, their brains have to RE-learn how to walk on Earth! That's how important these basic skills are. 🚀

4
Try It
Locomotor Challenge

Pick any room in your house — your bedroom, the living room, even your hallway. Now try crossing it in 5 different ways:

  1. Walk across
  2. Hop across on one foot
  3. Skip across
  4. Gallop across like a horse
  5. Slide across (sideways!)
🏃Activity Cue

Bonus: Try going backwards! Walking backwards, hopping backwards, sliding backwards — they all use different brain skills than going forwards. Watch out for furniture! 🛋️

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Locomotor — Movement that helps your body travel.
  • Balance — Staying steady while moving.
  • Coordination — Brain and body working smoothly together.
  • Hop — Jump on ONE foot, land on the SAME foot.
  • Gallop — One foot leads, the other follows.
  • Slide — Sideways movement, feet stay close to the ground.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflection: Which locomotor skill is your favorite and why? Which one was the trickiest? Did you laugh while trying any of them? 📝

→What's Next

Coming up: Week 13 Discussion, then in Week 14 you'll log your favorite locomotor moves in your own movement journal!

pages.title: Week 15: Throwing & Catching
pages.html:
Optima
Academy Online
Mission: Move!
3rd Grade PE · Unit 1.8 · Throwing & Catching
Week 15

Throwing & Catching: Aim, Toss, Snag! 🎯

Whenever you toss a beanbag, catch a frisbee, or aim a basketball — you're using "manipulative skills." Big words, simple meaning: you're using your hands (or feet) to control an object. Let's level up your aim!

1
Lesson 1
What Are Manipulative Skills?

Manipulative skills are anytime you use your body to move and control an object — like a ball, beanbag, frisbee, paddle, or even a hockey stick.

Today we're zooming in on TWO of the most important ones:

  • 🤾 Throwing — Sending an object through the air to a target
  • 🙌 Catching — Grabbing an object that's coming toward you
2
Lesson 2
How Does Throwing Work?

Throwing isn't just about your arm. It's a WHOLE body skill!

👀
Your Eyes
Lock onto the target.
🦶
Your Feet
Step toward the target as you throw.
💪
Your Arm
Pull back, then snap forward.
🌀
Your Hips
Twist! That's where the power comes from.
💡Did You Know?

Humans are basically the BEST throwers in the animal kingdom. 🦍 Even the strongest gorilla can't throw nearly as accurately as you can! Why? Our shoulders are built for it. Cool, right? 🦴

3
Lesson 3
How Does Catching Work?

Catching is teamwork between your eyes, your hands, and your brain. Here's the trick:

  1. 👀 Track the object with your eyes the WHOLE time
  2. 🙌 Get your hands in position EARLY
  3. 🤲 Form a "soft basket" with your hands (cup them gently)
  4. 🎯 As the object arrives, pull it gently into your body

This is called hand-eye coordination — your eyes tell your hands exactly where to go!

🏃Activity Cue

Try it: Crumple a piece of paper into a ball. Toss it up and catch it with two hands. Then try one hand! Then try while spinning around (carefully!). 🌀

4
Lesson 4
Why These Skills Matter

Throwing and catching show up EVERYWHERE:

  • 🏀 Basketball — passing and shooting
  • ⚾ Baseball / softball — throwing and catching ALL the time
  • 🥏 Frisbee — fancy throws
  • ⚽ Even soccer goalies catch with their hands!
  • 🎯 Cornhole, beanbag toss, dodgeball

Plus, your arms and shoulders get strong, and your brain gets quicker at reacting.

🌎Real-World Connection

Want to know a secret? The BEST throwers and catchers practice every single day — but never with super heavy objects. They start with soft balls, beanbags, or even rolled-up socks. You can practice at home with anything safe and squishy! 🧦

5
Lesson 5
Words to Know
  • Manipulative Skills — Using hands or feet to move an object.
  • Throw — Sending an object through the air.
  • Catch — Grabbing an object that's coming toward you.
  • Hand-Eye Coordination — Eyes and hands working together.
  • Target — The spot or person you're aiming for.
  • Aim — Pointing your throw exactly where you want it to go.
📝Weekly Reflection

Reflect: Are you a better thrower or catcher? Why do you think? What's the silliest thing you've ever thrown? 📝

→What's Next

How to do it:

Forearm Plank

How to do it:

  • Get into a plank position with forearms on the ground and back flat.
  • Hold for 30 seconds without dropping your belly.
  • Challenge: Try tapping one shoulder at a time while holding the plank.
  • Modification: Try a knee plank if needed.

Benefits: Builds core and upper body strength.

Push-Ups

How to do it:

  • Start by lying on your stomach with your hands flat on the floor next to your shoulders.
  • Push your body up so your arms are straight and only your hands and toes are touching the ground.
  • Keep your body in a straight line — don't let your back sag or your hips rise.
  • Bend your elbows and lower your body until your chest is close to the floor, then push back up.
  • Try 5 push-ups to start.

Benefits: Builds upper body strength.

Week 14 Flight Club: Power Up! 🦸

🚀 Flight Club Challenge

Time to feel STRONG. Three power moves to make your muscles cheer. Heroes, assemble! 💪

1
Split Squat

How to do it:

  • Stand up tall with one foot in front and the other foot behind you — like you're about to take a big step.
  • Keep your front knee over your ankle and your back heel lifted off the ground.
  • Slowly bend both knees to lower your body straight down.
  • Stop when your back knee is close to the ground (but not touching!).
  • Stand back up.
  • Do 5 slow squats, then switch legs and repeat.

Benefits: Strengthens leg muscles, especially thighs and calves.

2
Superhero Hold (Superman)

How to do it:

  • Lie flat on your stomach on the floor or a soft mat.
  • Stretch your arms straight out in front of you and your legs straight behind you.
  • At the same time, lift your arms, chest, and legs slightly off the ground.
  • Try to hold this pose for 10 seconds — like you're flying through the sky! 🦸
  • Slowly lower back down and rest.
  • Try it again 2–3 more times!

Benefits: Strengthens back and core muscles.

3
Bench Dips

How to do it:

  • Find a sturdy chair, bench, or low table.
  • Sit on the edge with your hands next to your hips.
  • Walk your feet forward and slide your bottom off the edge, so your hands are holding you up.
  • Bend your elbows to lower your body a little — like you're going down slowly.
  • Push back up until your arms are straight again.
  • Try doing 5–10 dips, then take a break!

Benefits: Strengthens arms, shoulders, and chest.

Yell really loud at the sky 🗣️

questions.text: Why is it a good idea to COOL DOWN after exercising?

answers.text: So you can practice falling asleep 💤
So your heart rate slowly returns to normal and your muscles relax 😌
It's a rule from outer space 🛸

questions.text: Physical activity helps your brain feel happier and more focused.
What's the name of the muscle that pumps blood around your body? (Hint: it has 4 letters and beats inside your chest!) 💓

quizzes.description: Show what you've learned about why we move our bodies and how warm-ups get you ready! 5 questions. Try your best — and have FUN!

quizzes.title: Quiz 2: Strength & Cardio Power

questions.text: Which of these is a great way to build STRENGTH at home?
Which activity counts as CARDIO (gets your heart pumping)?
Why do we need STRONG muscles in everyday life?

answers.text: So we can lift cars like superheroes 🚗
To carry things, climb stairs, and play without getting tired 🎒
So we never have to use our brains 🧠
Because the law says we have to 📜

questions.text: You don't need a gym or fancy weights to build strength — your own body is a great tool!
Fill in the blank: When you do cardio, your heart and ____ work together to give your body oxygen. (4 letters — they help you breathe!)

quizzes.description: Time to check what you know about muscle strength and getting that heart pumping! 5 questions. You've got this! 💪

quizzes.title: Quiz 3: Flexibility & Healthy Eating

answers.text: How easily your body can bend, twist, and stretch 🤸

questions.text: Which is an example of a healthy BALANCED meal?

answers.text: A plate with veggies, fruit, grain, protein, AND dairy 🥗

questions.text: What does STRETCHING do for your body?

answers.text: It makes you grow a tail 🦝
It keeps your muscles loose and helps prevent injuries 🦋

discussions.title: Week 1: Why We Move
discussions.html:
Discussion Time! 🎉 Talk about WHY moving matters. Pick at least ONE question to answer, and reply to at least one classmate's post.

  • 💪 Why is exercise good for your heart?
  • 🤝 What does teamwork look like when you play games in PE?
  • 😄 How can physical activity help you feel better every day?

Tip: Real examples from YOUR life are the best — share a story!

discussions.title: Week 3: Warm-Ups & Cool-Downs
discussions.html:
Warm-Up Discussion 🔥

Now that you've learned about warm-ups and cool-downs, share with your classmates!

  • Why is warming up SO important before exercise?
  • What's YOUR favorite warm-up move and why?
  • How do you feel during a cool-down? Calm? Sweaty? Tired in a good way?

Reply to at least one classmate and add something new — a tip, an idea, or just a "I love that move too!"

discussions.title: Week 5: Muscular Strength
discussions.html:
Strength Talk 💪

Strong muscles make life easier. Pick a question to discuss with your class:

  • What's something heavy you can lift now that you COULDN'T lift a year ago?
  • Which strength exercise sounds the most fun to try? Why?
  • Why do you think we need strong muscles in everyday life (not just sports)?

discussions.title: Week 7: Cardiovascular Fitness
discussions.html:
Cardio Chat ❤️

  • What's YOUR favorite way to do cardio? (Running? Dancing? Biking? Tag?)
  • How can you tell when your cardio system is working? (Hint: heart, lungs, sweat!)
  • What's one new cardio activity you'd be brave enough to try this month?

Reply to a classmate's post — bonus points for cheering them on!

discussions.title: Week 9: Flexibility & Stretching
discussions.html:
Flexibility Discussion 🤸

  • What part of your body is the LEAST flexible? (Be honest — most people have a tight spot!)
  • What's the silliest stretch you've ever done?
  • How does stretching make you feel — physically and mentally?

discussions.title: Week 11: Nutrition
discussions.html:
Nutrition Talk 🍎

  • What's your FAVORITE healthy food? Why?
  • What's the silliest healthy food you've ever tried? Did you like it?
  • What food group do you eat the MOST of? The LEAST of?

Be respectful — everyone eats different things, and that's okay!

discussions.title: Week 13: Locomotor Skills
discussions.html:
Locomotor Discussion 🚀

  • Which locomotor skill is the EASIEST for you? Which is the HARDEST?
  • Have you ever invented a new way to move? Describe it!
  • Why do you think babies have to LEARN how to walk?

discussions.title: Week 15: Throwing & Catching
discussions.html:
Throw & Catch Talk 🎯

  • Are you a better thrower or catcher? Why do you think?
  • What's the most amazing catch you've ever made (or seen)?
  • Why is hand-eye coordination important — even outside of sports?
